name: Jacqueline (Jacquie) Fleisig
title: 4th Year Medical Student @ University of Toronto
bio:
Jacquie Fleisig is a fourth-year medical student at the University of Toronto. Prior to medical school, she completed her Bachelor's of Applied Science in Engineering Science (Biomedical Systems Option) at the University of Toronto. During her undergrad, she was never certain about where her career would end up but did know she loved any type of problem-solving. She discovered she enjoyed leading teams through her involvement in the Skule community, serving as president of Engineers Without Borders UofT and president of the Engineering Society at different times.
Her Professional Experience Year was a mix of jobs: four months working on a novel fluorescence-guided surgery system, four months in neuronal network simulation research, and eight months in operations consulting. After that, she applied to medical school at UofT where she is now.
In medical school, she has realized her passion for working with patients of all different backgrounds and developed an interest in health services research, which she hopes to continue building on throughout her career. She is excited to speak to WISE attendees about her path, what she has learned, and what is next!

name: Carmela De Luca
title: Principal @ Smart & Biggar LP
bio:
Carmela is a lawyer and registered patent agent in Canada and the United States and practices in all areas of intellectual property, focusing on patent matters, particularly for life science companies. She advises clients on strategic global aspects of obtaining and managing patent portfolios, as well as in the preparation and procurement of patents and industrial designs. She works closely with clients including start-ups, universities as well as multinationals in preparing and prosecuting patent applications relating to biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, biologics, diagnostics, green technologies and other areas in the life sciences. Carmela is also active in the analysis of patent issues such as validity, infringement and freedom to operate.
While obtaining her Ph.D. from McGill University, Carmela conducted research in the areas of inflammation, signal transduction and virology. Prior to earning a law degree, Carmela worked as a post-doctoral fellow at a research institute of an international biotechnology company where her research focused on cancer cell biology, genetic engineering, genetic screens and genomics. Her educational and research background provides her with a depth of knowledge and experiences to assist her clients in a wide range of cutting-edge technologies.

name: Michela Trozzo
title: High School Physics Teacher @ Toronto Catholic District School Board
bio: Michela brings a unique and robust background to her teaching career, rooted in her foundational studies in Electrical Engineering at the University of Toronto. Prior to her career transition, she cultivated her passion for education by engaging with high school students through various STEAM outreach programs offered by the University of Toronto Engineering Outreach Office and Hi-Skule™ Project Directorship. These experiences allowed her to teach Grades 7-12 students on specialized topics; including robotics, coding, physics, and mathematics. Recognizing her dedication to teaching, Michela completed her Bachelor of Education at York University after her engineering studies. She is now a qualified high school teacher specializing in Mathematics, Physics, and Computer Science. Currently, she teaches Grade 11 and 12 University Bound and College Bound Physics. Beyond the classroom, Michela serves as a mentor for her school's robotics club, where she guides the next generation of engineers. She is notably proud of the team's recent success, which includes achieving third place in last year's school board competition.

name: Rachel Geddam
title: Environmental Engineer @ Thurber Engineering Ltd.
bio:
I hold a Bachelor of Engineering (B.Eng.) in Civil Engineering from York University. I've worked in the consulting industry for over 4 years now and I am now a Licensed Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) in Ontario with 4.5+ years of experience in environmental engineering, specializing in environmental site assessments, excess soil management - regulatory compliance under Ontario Regulations 153/04 and 406/19.
My work focuses on supporting large-scale infrastructure and development projects across the GTA, including municipal roadways, and rail corridors and provide expertise in Phase I & II ESAs, and Soil Management Plans. My experience spans working with municipalities, regional authorities, and private developers, often in collaboration with multidisciplinary teams.
I also have experience in hydrogeology, including groundwater assessments, dewatering evaluations and estimates, Environmental Activity and Sector Registry (EASR) registrations, Permit to Take Water (PTTW) support, and groundwater quality assessment and interpretation.

name: Suzanne Appleton
title: Director Personal Conduct Data Systems & Chief of Professional Conduct and Culture @ Royal Canadian Navy
bio: Suzanne is a Captain in the Royal Canadian Navy in the Naval Engineer occupation, with a background in marine systems. Her love for the sea and the marine environment were fostered at a young age but really solidified during her time as a teenager with the Toronto Brigantine Tall Ship sail training program. Throughout her career, Suzanne has had the privilege of gaining extensive technical leadership experience through roles such as head of the engineering department at sea onboard HMCS Winnipeg, numerous projects and programs on topics relating to ships, technical trials, HR, Environmental, IT and innovation. This professional path contributes to ensuring that RCN sailors have the equipment and systems they need to protect and secure Canada's three coasts. Some of her career highlights include migrant vessel interdictions, Search and Rescue, multinational exercises, representing Canada at NATO fora, advancing women and BIPOC in STEM, and being part of an award-winning project team.
